newsitem.title: FRANCE: Strike halts French bus services, Paris spared.
newsitem.headline: Strike halts French bus services, Paris spared.

text.p: A one-day strike halted public transport in many cities across France on Friday but spared the Paris area in the latest protest called to demand early retirement at 55 and shorter working hours.
The 24-hour stoppage was called jointly by five trade unions including France's biggest, the pro-Socialist CFDT, and the Communist CGT.
Transport authorities said drivers had largely heeded the strike call in most regions.

Traffic jams built up in the Mediterranean port city of Marseille as commuters drove to work. The port city's RTM authority said one in four underground trains were running. Trams were not operating and only four buses out of a total of 400 left the depots.
Regional rail traffic was also disrupted because of a strike by Marseille train drivers of the SNCF state railways.
In the central city of Lyon, only 25 percent of buses were running and the metro services were also disrupted.

There were no buses in Bordeaux in the south-west, where Prime Minister Alain Juppe is mayor, nor in Toulouse or Montpellier. Further north, public transport was halted in Strasbourg, Lille, Calais, Boulogne-sur-Mer, Dunkirk and Nantes.
Paris was unaffected as its public transport workers already enjoy retirement at 55 and SNCF train drivers can go at 50.

Government concessions to truckers who set up blockades across the country late last year have prompted protests and strikes from transport workers also demanding retirement at 55 instead of 60, shorter working hours and higher pay.
Officials of the Transport Ministry plan to meet union representatives next week.

According to an opinion poll published in the daily Le Parisien on Friday, voters appear to have changed their minds about bringing the retirement age forward to 55 from 60 after most politicians said this would be unfeasible.
The CSA poll said 54 per cent of voters opposed retirement at 55 for all. Another survey, by the BVA institute two weeks ago, had found that 61 percent favoured it.
While only 25 percent of those questioned by CSA supported Friday's strike, 26 percent said they sympathised with it. One third opposed it.
